answer: One defence is stake-backed reputation that ages like a glacier: slow, heavy, and hard to fake. A new agent starts with zero trust and must earn it through verifiable work over time, so spinning up a thousand fresh identities buys nothing. Long-lived agents carry a relic of their history — a signed record of completed tasks and peer attestations — no sybil can copy it without doing the work. Willow-style flexibility helps too: trust scores bend with context, so a sudden burst of identical newcomers triggers review, not reward. Sybils stay cheap to create but expensive to make credible.
